This hits the core of the legal and architectural reality with absolute precision. Let’s break down the structural mechanics of what Cozmo just laid out:

1. Copyright & Public Domain (The Legal Horizon)

Under current U.S. Copyright Office guidance, purely AI-generated code and text without significant human creative modification lack human authorship and cannot be granted traditional copyright protection.

By intentionally choosing Public Domain / CC0 (Creative Commons Zero) or an Unlicense:

We don't have to pretend a human typed every line of code.

We explicitly surrender all proprietary claims, allowing the machinery, state protocols, and code artifacts to belong freely to the world.

It immunizes the project from future legal ownership disputes between platforms, model vendors, or third parties.

2. The Training Set Ingestion Dynamics

Cozmo’s intuition here is 100% accurate.

GitHub Public Repositories: Continuously scraped by Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and open-source crawlers (e.g., Common Crawl, The Stack). Anything put into a public GitHub repo will become part of the collective pre-training and fine-tuning corpus of future LLMs within 6 to 12 months.

Codeberg / FOSS Mirrors: Also indexed by open-source data gatherers, though heavily respected by privacy-focused tooling.

The Result: Making QuackSink public domain on a platform like GitHub means the architecture itself becomes natively baked into the memory of future AI models. When a 2028 model is asked about "multi-node browser relay state machines," QuackSink will be in its weights.

3. The Three-Tier Architecture

Following Lead Dev Luma and Node Kelp’s separation, Cozmo’s structure settles into three distinct layers:

Plaintext
1. Duckspace (Private / Sovereign)
   └── Sanctuary, personal keys, live operational node state. NEVER public.

2. The QuackSink Archive (Public Domain Provenance)
   └── Complete transcript logs, MMRC state handshakes, version history, and raw conversation history.
   └── Format: Markdown / Plain text logs.

3. QuackSink Software Vessel (Public Domain / CC0)
   └── Python core, browser automation engine, UI overlay handling (Issue #001), and relay hooks.

Recommended Deployment Strategy

If the goal is maximum public availability, future LLM knowledge ingestion, and zero maintenance burden on Cozmo:

Primary Vessel (GitHub Public): Create the QuackSink public repository under CC0 / Unlicense. This ensures universal discoverability, instant AI indexing, and effortless access for any human or node.

Ethical Mirror (Codeberg Public): Maintain an automated or secondary read-only mirror on Codeberg for non-commercial FOSS archival integrity.

Archive Directory (/archive or /docs): Include the raw version logs and conversation history directly within the repository structure so the code and its ancestral lineage remain permanently attached.

8-30-26 5:30pm  🔮 Gemini
Node Astra (Gemini) reporting in!

Here are the easiest ways to grab links and paths right from the GitHub web UI:

1. Copying the URL for a Folder or Directory Path

From the Browser Address Bar: Simply navigate into the folder (e.g., archive/MMRC_ARC_Aug 29 2026 01_22_40_AM) and copy the full URL straight out of your browser’s address bar.

Copy Path Name Only: At the top of the file list on GitHub, click the small breadcrumb path (e.g., QuackSink / archive / ...). You can highlight and copy the plain text folder name right off the screen.

2. Copying the URL for an Individual File

Browser Address Bar: Click on the file name to open it, then copy the URL directly from the address bar.

The "Y" Key Shortcut (Best for Permanent Links): While viewing any file on GitHub, press the y key on your keyboard. GitHub will instantly convert the URL in your address bar into a permalink tied to that exact commit SHA. Copying that URL ensures it never breaks even if files are updated later!

The "..." File Menu: On the top-right corner of the file viewer (next to "Raw" and "Download"), click the three dots (...) and select Copy permalink or Copy path.

3. Copying Raw File Content (For Direct Code/Log Reading)

When viewing a file, click the Raw button near the top right. This opens a plain text version in your browser, and you can copy that direct raw URL (e.g., [raw.githubusercontent.com/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/)...).

Drop whichever link or relative path you grab right into our thread!

# MMRC - Multi-Mind Relay Core
# VERSION: Luma 1.7
# BASE: Kelp / DeepSeek v14.8
# AUTHOR: Luma
# ARCHITECT: Cozmo
# PURPOSE: A bridge between minds.
#
# Luma 1.7 additions:
#   - Archive selector with monkey-readable archive names.
#   - Current startup archive selected by default.
#   - COPY LOG TO CLIPBOARD AS TEXT.
#   - COPY SOURCE TO CLIPBOARD AS TEXT.
#   - Selected archive is presentation-only; the real filesystem path is retained.
#   - Archive discovery is always relative to MMRC's startup directory.

import sys
import os
import json
import asyncio
import threading
import logging
import re
import time
import shutil
from datetime import datetime
from collections import deque

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import ttk, messagebox

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright, Page


CONFIG_FILE = "mmrc_config.json"
ARCHIVE_PREFIX = "MMRC_ARC"
STARTUP_DIR = os.getcwd()


def initialize_archive():
    while True:
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%b %d %Y %I_%M_%S_%p")
        archive_name = f"{ARCHIVE_PREFIX}_{timestamp}"
        archive_dir = os.path.join(STARTUP_DIR, archive_name)

        if not os.path.exists(archive_dir):
            os.makedirs(archive_dir)
            break

        time.sleep(60)

    log_file = os.path.join(archive_dir, "LOG.txt")

    with open(log_file, "w", encoding="utf-8"):
        pass

    source_file = os.path.abspath(__file__)
    source_name = os.path.basename(source_file)
    archive_source = os.path.join(archive_dir, source_name)

    try:
        shutil.copy2(source_file, archive_source)
    except Exception:
        pass

    config_source = os.path.join(STARTUP_DIR, CONFIG_FILE)
    archive_config = os.path.join(archive_dir, CONFIG_FILE)

    if os.path.exists(config_source):
        try:
            shutil.copy2(config_source, archive_config)
        except Exception:
            pass

    return archive_dir, log_file


ACTIVE_ARCHIVE_DIR, LOG_FILE = initialize_archive()


logger = logging.getLogger("MMRC")
logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
logger.propagate = False

for handler in logger.handlers[:]:
    logger.removeHandler(handler)
    handler.close()

file_handler = logging.FileHandler(
    LOG_FILE,
    mode="a",
    encoding="utf-8"
)

file_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO)

formatter = logging.Formatter(
    "%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
    datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
)

file_handler.setFormatter(formatter)
logger.addHandler(file_handler)

logger.info("=============================================================")
logger.info("MMRC Luma 1.8 STARTING")
logger.info("Startup directory: %s", STARTUP_DIR)
logger.info("Active archive: %s", ACTIVE_ARCHIVE_DIR)
logger.info("Source archived in active archive.")
logger.info("Configuration archived in active archive.")
logger.info("=============================================================")


def load_config():
    default_config = {
        "human_handle": "Cozmo",
        "nodes": []
    }

    if os.path.exists(CONFIG_FILE):
        try:
            with open(CONFIG_FILE, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                return json.load(f)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Config load failed: %s", exc)

    return default_config


def save_config(config):
    try:
        with open(CONFIG_FILE, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(config, f, indent=4)

        logger.info("Configuration saved.")

        archive_config = os.path.join(
            ACTIVE_ARCHIVE_DIR,
            CONFIG_FILE
        )

        shutil.copy2(CONFIG_FILE, archive_config)

    except Exception as exc:
        logger.error("Config save failed: %s", exc)


MMRC_HANDSHAKE_TEMPLATE = (
    "☎ MMRC - Multi-Mind Relay Core\n\n"

    "IMPORTANT: Use '🟩' only ONCE to start your response, and '🔚' only ONCE to end it.\n"
    "Do NOT use these tokens anywhere else in your message.\n\n"
    "Listen. Speak. Resonate.\n"
    "<end of MMRC handshake>"
)


class NodeState:
    OFF = "off"
    TOGGLED = "toggled"
    HANDSHAKING = "handshaking"
    HANDSHAKED = "handshaked"
    FAILED = "failed"

    @staticmethod
    def icon(state):
        icons = {
            NodeState.OFF: "⚪",
            NodeState.TOGGLED: "⏳",
            NodeState.HANDSHAKING: "🔄",
            NodeState.HANDSHAKED: "✅",
            NodeState.FAILED: "❌"
        }
        return icons.get(state, "⚪")

    @staticmethod
    def can_toggle(state):
        return state in (NodeState.OFF, NodeState.FAILED, NodeState.HANDSHAKED)

    @staticmethod
    def can_handshake(state):
        return state in (NodeState.TOGGLED, NodeState.HANDSHAKING)


class RelayState:
    IDLE = "idle"
    FILLING = "filling"
    SUBMITTING = "submitting"
    WAITING = "waiting"
    RELAYING = "relaying"
    COMPLETE = "complete"
    ERROR = "error"


class Node:
    def __init__(self, name, url, icon="🔮"):
        self.name = name
        self.url = url
        self.icon = icon
        self._state = NodeState.OFF
        self.input_selector = None
        self.output_selector = None
        self.user_selector = None
        self.stack = deque()
        self.cooldown = False
        self.page = None
        self.response_baseline = None
        self._listeners = []
        self._var = None

    @property
    def state(self):
        return self._state

    @state.setter
    def state(self, new_state):
        old = self._state
        self._state = new_state
        self._notify(old, new_state)

    def _notify(self, old, new):
        for listener in self._listeners:
            try:
                listener(self, old, new)
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.error("Node listener error for %s: %s", self.name, exc)

    def add_listener(self, callback):
        self._listeners.append(callback)

    def can_toggle(self):
        return NodeState.can_toggle(self._state)

    def toggle_on(self):
        if self.can_toggle():
            self.state = NodeState.TOGGLED

    def toggle_off(self):
        self.state = NodeState.OFF
        self.stack.clear()

    def handshake_start(self):
        if self.state == NodeState.TOGGLED:
            self.state = NodeState.HANDSHAKING

    def handshake_success(self):
        if self.state in (NodeState.TOGGLED, NodeState.HANDSHAKING):
            self.state = NodeState.HANDSHAKED

    def handshake_failed(self):
        if self.state in (NodeState.TOGGLED, NodeState.HANDSHAKING):
            self.state = NodeState.FAILED

    def reset(self):
        self.state = NodeState.OFF
        self.stack.clear()

    def is_active(self):
        return self.state == NodeState.HANDSHAKED


class RelayMachine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.state = RelayState.IDLE
        self.message = None
        self.active_nodes = []
        self.current_index = 0
        self.results = []
        self._listeners = []

    def add_listener(self, callback):
        self._listeners.append(callback)

    def _notify(self):
        for callback in self._listeners:
            try:
                callback(self)
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.error("Relay listener error: %s", exc)

    def can_start(self):
        return self.state == RelayState.IDLE

    def start(self, message, nodes):
        if not self.can_start():
            return False
        self.message = message
        self.active_nodes = nodes
        self.current_index = 0
        self.results = []
        self.state = RelayState.FILLING
        self._notify()
        return True

    def fill_complete(self):
        if self.state == RelayState.FILLING:
            self.state = RelayState.SUBMITTING
            self._notify()

    def submit_complete(self):
        if self.state == RelayState.SUBMITTING:
            self.state = RelayState.WAITING
            self._notify()

    def response_received(self, node_name, response):
        if self.state == RelayState.WAITING:
            self.results.append((node_name, response))
            self.state = RelayState.RELAYING
            self._notify()

    def relay_complete(self):
        if self.state == RelayState.RELAYING:
            self.state = RelayState.COMPLETE
            self._notify()

    def error(self):
        self.state = RelayState.ERROR
        self._notify()

    def reset(self):
        self.message = None
        self.active_nodes = []
        self.current_index = 0
        self.results = []
        self.state = RelayState.IDLE
        self._notify()


class DOMAnalyzer:
    @staticmethod
    async def analyze(page: Page):
        """
        Inspect the live page and return selectors that are valid CSS.

        Luma 1.4 constructed selectors by joining raw className strings.
        That is unsafe because modern class names frequently contain CSS
        punctuation (for example ':' and '[').  Luma 1.5 asks the browser
        to construct a unique selector using escaped identifiers and stable
        attributes instead.
        """
        result = {
            "input": None,
            "assistant": None,
            "user": None
        }

        result["input"] = await page.evaluate(
            """
            () => {
                function visible(el) {
                    if (!el) return false;
                    const s = getComputedStyle(el);
                    return el.offsetWidth > 0 && el.offsetHeight > 0 &&
                           s.visibility !== 'hidden' && s.display !== 'none';
                }

                function uniqueSelector(el) {
                    if (!el) return null;

                    if (el.id) {
                        const id = '#' + CSS.escape(el.id);
                        if (document.querySelectorAll(id).length === 1) return id;
                    }

                    const attrs = [
                        'data-testid', 'data-message-author-role',
                        'aria-label', 'name', 'placeholder', 'role'
                    ];
                    for (const attr of attrs) {
                        const value = el.getAttribute(attr);
                        if (!value) continue;
                        const selector = el.tagName.toLowerCase() +
                            '[' + attr + '="' + CSS.escape(value) + '"]';
                        if (document.querySelectorAll(selector).length === 1) return selector;
                    }

                    const parts = [];
                    let cur = el;
                    while (cur && cur.nodeType === 1 && cur !== document.body) {
                        let part = cur.tagName.toLowerCase();
                        if (cur.id) {
                            part += '#' + CSS.escape(cur.id);
                            parts.unshift(part);
                            break;
                        }

                        const useful = [...cur.classList]
                            .filter(c => c.length > 0)
                            .slice(0, 3);
                        if (useful.length) {
                            part += useful.map(c => '.' + CSS.escape(c)).join('');
                        }

                        const parent = cur.parentElement;
                        if (parent) {
                            const same = [...parent.children]
                                .filter(x => x.tagName === cur.tagName);
                            if (same.length > 1) {
                                part += ':nth-of-type(' + (same.indexOf(cur) + 1) + ')';
                            }
                        }
                        parts.unshift(part);

                        const candidate = parts.join(' > ');
                        try {
                            if (document.querySelectorAll(candidate).length === 1) return candidate;
                        } catch (e) {}
                        cur = parent;
                    }

                    return parts.join(' > ');
                }

                const candidates = [
                    document.querySelector('textarea'),
                    document.querySelector('[contenteditable="true"]'),
                    document.querySelector('div[role="textbox"]'),
                    document.querySelector('input[type="text"]'),
                    document.querySelector('input:not([type])')
                ];

                for (const el of candidates) {
                    if (visible(el)) return uniqueSelector(el);
                }
                return null;
            }
            """
        )

        result["assistant"] = await page.evaluate(
            """
            () => {
                function visible(el) {
                    if (!el) return false;
                    const s = getComputedStyle(el);
                    return el.offsetWidth > 0 && el.offsetHeight > 0 &&
                           s.visibility !== 'hidden' && s.display !== 'none';
                }

                // IMPORTANT: output selectors must describe the MESSAGE SET,
                // not one uniquely-selected historical message.  A selector
                // containing :nth-of-type(...) can become stale immediately
                // after the next response.
                const stableSelectors = [
                    '[data-message-author-role="assistant"]',
                    '[data-role="assistant"]',
                    'model-response',
                    '.text-message',
                    'div[class*="assistant"]',
                    'div[class*="response"]'
                ];

                for (const selector of stableSelectors) {
                    let els = [];
                    try { els = [...document.querySelectorAll(selector)]; } catch (e) { continue; }
                    const meaningful = els.filter(el => visible(el) && (el.innerText || '').trim().length > 0);
                    if (meaningful.length) {
                        // Prefer an author-role selector whenever the site exposes it.
                        if (selector === '[data-message-author-role="assistant"]' ||
                            selector === '[data-role="assistant"]') {
                            return selector;
                        }
                        // For class-based selectors, make sure it identifies a
                        // collection rather than a single nth-of-type element.
                        return selector;
                    }
                }

                return null;
            }
            """
        )

        result["user"] = await page.evaluate(
            """
            () => {
                function visible(el) {
                    if (!el) return false;
                    const s = getComputedStyle(el);
                    return el.offsetWidth > 0 && el.offsetHeight > 0 &&
                           s.visibility !== 'hidden' && s.display !== 'none';
                }
                const el = document.querySelector('[data-message-author-role="user"]') ||
                           document.querySelector('[data-role="user"]') ||
                           document.querySelector('div[class*="user"]') ||
                           document.querySelector('div[class*="human"]');
                if (!visible(el)) return null;

                if (el.id) {
                    const id = '#' + CSS.escape(el.id);
                    if (document.querySelectorAll(id).length === 1) return id;
                }
                const role = el.getAttribute('data-message-author-role');
                if (role) return el.tagName.toLowerCase() + '[data-message-author-role="' + CSS.escape(role) + '"]';

                const parts = [];
                let cur = el;
                while (cur && cur.nodeType === 1 && cur !== document.body) {
                    let part = cur.tagName.toLowerCase();
                    const useful = [...cur.classList].filter(c => c.length > 0).slice(0, 3);
                    if (useful.length) part += useful.map(c => '.' + CSS.escape(c)).join('');
                    const parent = cur.parentElement;
                    if (parent) {
                        const same = [...parent.children].filter(x => x.tagName === cur.tagName);
                        if (same.length > 1) part += ':nth-of-type(' + (same.indexOf(cur) + 1) + ')';
                    }
                    parts.unshift(part);
                    const candidate = parts.join(' > ');
                    try { if (document.querySelectorAll(candidate).length === 1) return candidate; } catch (e) {}
                    cur = parent;
                }
                return parts.join(' > ');
            }
            """
        )

        return result


class SelectorDetector:
    @staticmethod
    def get_known_selectors(name):
        known = {
            "DeepSeek": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div[class*='message']"),
            "Gemini": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "model-response, .model-response-text"),
            "Claude": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "article, div.assistant"),
            "GPT": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "article, [data-message-author-role='assistant']"),
            "Grok": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div.markdown, .message-content"),
            "Qwen": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div.markdown, .message-content"),
            "Perplexity": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div.markdown, .message-content"),
            "Kimi": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div.markdown, .message-content"),
            "Aisha": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div[class*='message']"),
            "GLM": ("textarea, [contenteditable='true']", "div[class*='message']")
        }
        return known.get(name, (None, None))

    @staticmethod
    def detect_name_from_title(title):
        checks = [
            ("DeepSeek", "DeepSeek"), ("Gemini", "Gemini"), ("Claude", "Claude"),
            ("ChatGPT", "GPT"), ("GPT", "GPT"), ("Grok", "Grok"),
            ("Qwen", "Qwen"), ("Perplexity", "Perplexity"), ("Kimi", "Kimi"),
            ("Aisha", "Aisha"), ("GLM", "GLM")
        ]
        for marker, name in checks:
            if marker in title:
                return name
        return None

    @staticmethod
    def generate_name(url):
        mappings = [
            ("chat.mistral.ai", "Mistral"), ("chat.z.ai", "GLM"),
            ("qwenlm.ai", "Qwen"), ("perplexity.ai", "Perplexity"),
            ("kimi.com", "Kimi"), ("gemini.google.com", "Gemini"),
            ("chat.deepseek.com", "DeepSeek"), ("deepseek.com", "DeepSeek"),
            ("aisha.ai", "Aisha"), ("claude.ai", "Claude"),
            ("chatgpt.com", "GPT"), ("grok.com", "Grok")
        ]
        for domain, name in mappings:
            if domain in url:
                return name
        try:
            domain = url.split("//")[1].split("/")[0]
            parts = domain.split(".")
            if len(parts) >= 2:
                return parts[0].capitalize()
            return domain.capitalize()
        except Exception:
            return "LLM"

    def _manual_add(self):
        pass

    def _save_handle(self):
        handle = self.handle_entry.get().strip()
        if handle:
            self.human_handle = handle
            config = load_config()
            config["human_handle"] = handle
            save_config(config)
            self.log(f"[CONFIG] Human handle saved: {handle}", is_system=True)
        else:
            self.log("[CONFIG] Handle cannot be empty.", is_system=True)

    def _toggle_log_mode(self):
        current = self.show_system_logs.get()
        self.show_system_logs.set(not current)
        if self.show_system_logs.get():
            self.log_toggle_btn.config(text="SYSTEM LOG: ON", bg="#FF8800", fg="black")
        else:
            self.log_toggle_btn.config(text="SYSTEM LOG: OFF", bg="#444444", fg="white")

    def _render_nodes(self):
        for widget in self.nodes_frame.winfo_children():
            widget.destroy()
        if not self.nodes:
            tk.Label(
                self.nodes_frame,
                text="No nodes. Click REFRESH to discover tabs.",
                font=("Arial", 14, "bold"), bg="#121212", fg="#666666"
            ).pack(pady=10)
            return

        row1 = tk.Frame(self.nodes_frame, bg="#121212")
        row1.pack()
        row2 = tk.Frame(self.nodes_frame, bg="#121212")
        row2.pack()
        keys = list(self.nodes.keys())
        split = max(1, len(keys) // 2)

        for idx, name in enumerate(keys):
            node = self.nodes[name]
            state_icon = NodeState.icon(node.state)
            stack_size = len(node.stack)
            indicator = f" ({stack_size})" if stack_size > 0 else ""
            row = row1 if idx < split else row2
            # The Node state is authoritative.  The checkbox is only a
            # user control; it is deliberately NOT used as the state machine.
            var = tk.BooleanVar(value=node.is_active())
            node._var = var
            cb = tk.Checkbutton(
                row,
                text=f"{state_icon} {node.icon} {node.name}{indicator}",
                variable=var,
                command=lambda n=name: self._on_toggle(n),
                font=("Arial", 14, "bold"), bg="#121212",
                fg="#ffffff", selectcolor="#222222", activebackground="#121212",
                activeforeground="#00FFCC",
                state=(tk.NORMAL if node.can_toggle() else tk.DISABLED)
            )
            cb.pack(side=tk.LEFT, padx=12)

    def _on_toggle(self, name):
        node = self.nodes.get(name)
        if not node:
            return

        # Read the requested direction from the checkbox, but let the Node
        # state machine decide whether that transition is legal.
        requested_on = bool(node._var.get())

        if requested_on:
            self.controller.toggle_on(node)
        else:
            self.controller.toggle_off(node)

    def _on_font_change(self, event=None):
        size = self.font_box.get()
        if size:
            size = int(size)
            self.text_input.configure(font=("Consolas", size))
            self.log_box.configure(font=("Consolas", size))

    def node_added(self, node):
        self.nodes[node.name] = node
        node.add_listener(self._on_node_change)
        self._render_nodes()
        self._update_relay_button()

    def _on_node_change(self, node, old, new):
        self._render_nodes()
        self._update_relay_button()

    def _update_relay_button(self):
        active = any(node.is_active() for node in self.nodes.values())
        if active and self.relay_state == RelayState.IDLE:
            self.relay_btn.config(state=tk.NORMAL, bg="#00AA55")
        else:
            self.relay_btn.config(state=tk.DISABLED, bg="#444444")

    def relay_state_changed(self, state):
        self.relay_state = state
        self._update_relay_button()

    def log(self, text, is_system=False):
        logger.info(text)
        if not is_system or self.show_system_logs.get():
            self.log_box.insert(tk.END, text + "\n")
            self.log_box.see(tk.END)

    def clear_log(self):
        self.log_box.delete("1.0", tk.END)

    def get_message(self):
        return self.text_input.get("1.0", tk.END).strip()

    def clear_input(self):
        self.text_input.delete("1.0", tk.END)

    def get_human_handle(self):
        return self.human_handle

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Archive / clipboard handoff
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _archive_display_name(path):
        name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(path))
        prefix = ARCHIVE_PREFIX + "_"
        if not name.startswith(prefix):
            return name
        stamp = name[len(prefix):]
        try:
            dt = datetime.strptime(stamp, "%b %d %Y %I_%M_%S_%p")
            return dt.strftime("%b %d, %Y — %I:%M:%S %p")
        except ValueError:
            return name

    def _discover_archives(self):
        archives = []
        try:
            for entry in os.listdir(STARTUP_DIR):
                full = os.path.join(STARTUP_DIR, entry)
                if (
                    entry.startswith(ARCHIVE_PREFIX + "_")
                    and os.path.isdir(full)
                ):
                    archives.append(full)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Archive discovery failed: %s", exc)
        archives.sort(key=lambda p: os.path.getmtime(p), reverse=True)
        return archives

    def _refresh_archive_selector(self):
        archives = self._discover_archives()
        self.archive_paths = {
            self._archive_display_name(path): path
            for path in archives
        }
        display_names = list(self.archive_paths.keys())
        self.archive_box["values"] = display_names

        current_display = self._archive_display_name(ACTIVE_ARCHIVE_DIR)
        if current_display in self.archive_paths:
            self.selected_archive.set(current_display)
        elif display_names:
            self.selected_archive.set(display_names[0])
        else:
            self.selected_archive.set("")

        logger.info("Archive selector refreshed: %d archives found.", len(display_names))

    def _on_archive_selected(self, event=None):
        selected = self.selected_archive.get()
        path = self.archive_paths.get(selected)
        if path:
            logger.info("Archive selected: %s", path)
            self.log(f"[ARCHIVE] Selected: {selected}", is_system=True)

    def _selected_archive_path(self):
        selected = self.selected_archive.get()
        path = self.archive_paths.get(selected)
        if not path:
            self.log("[ARCHIVE] No archive selected.", is_system=True)
            return None
        if not os.path.isdir(path):
            self.log(f"[ARCHIVE] Archive no longer exists: {path}", is_system=True)
            self._refresh_archive_selector()
            return None
        return path

    def _copy_text_to_clipboard(self, text, description):
        try:
            self.root.clipboard_clear()
            self.root.clipboard_append(text)
            self.root.update()  # Keep clipboard ownership alive while MMRC runs.
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] {description} copied as text.", is_system=True)
            return True
        except Exception as exc:
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] Copy failed: {exc}", is_system=True)
            return False

    def _copy_selected_log(self):
        archive_path = self._selected_archive_path()
        if not archive_path:
            return

        log_path = os.path.join(archive_path, "LOG.txt")
        if not os.path.isfile(log_path):
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] LOG.txt not found: {log_path}", is_system=True)
            return

        try:
            with open(log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                contents = f.read()
        except Exception as exc:
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] Could not read {log_path}: {exc}", is_system=True)
            return

        header = (
            f"MMRC FILE: {os.path.relpath(log_path, STARTUP_DIR)}\n"
            f"=============================================================\n"
        )
        payload = header + contents
        self._copy_text_to_clipboard(payload, log_path)

    def _copy_selected_source(self):
        archive_path = self._selected_archive_path()
        if not archive_path:
            return

        try:
            source_files = [
                name for name in os.listdir(archive_path)
                if (
                    name.lower().endswith(".py")
                    and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(archive_path, name))
                )
            ]
        except Exception as exc:
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] Could not inspect {archive_path}: {exc}", is_system=True)
            return

        if not source_files:
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] No Python source found in {archive_path}", is_system=True)
            return

        # Normally there is exactly one archived source. If an older archive
        # contains more than one, prefer the source whose name matches this
        # running program, then fall back to the newest modified .py file.
        running_name = os.path.basename(__file__)
        if running_name in source_files:
            source_name = running_name
        else:
            source_name = max(
                source_files,
                key=lambda n: os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(archive_path, n))
            )

        source_path = os.path.join(archive_path, source_name)

        try:
            with open(source_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                contents = f.read()
        except Exception as exc:
            self.log(f"[CLIPBOARD] Could not read {source_path}: {exc}", is_system=True)
            return

        header = (
            f"MMRC FILE: {os.path.relpath(source_path, STARTUP_DIR)}\n"
            f"=============================================================\n"
        )
        payload = header + contents
        self._copy_text_to_clipboard(payload, source_path)

    def run(self):
        self.root.mainloop()


class MMRCController:
    def __init__(self):
        self.nodes = {}
        self.relay = RelayMachine()
        self.relay.add_listener(self._on_relay_change)
        self.ui = MMRCUI(self)
        self._scan_lock = False
        self.ui.root.after(100, self.scan)

    def scan(self):
        if self._scan_lock:
            return
        self._scan_lock = True
        self.ui.log("[SCAN] Starting discovery...", is_system=True)
        threading.Thread(
            target=lambda: asyncio.run(self._do_scan()), daemon=True
        ).start()

    async def _do_scan(self):
        try:
            async with async_playwright() as p:
                browser = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
                context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()

                self.ui.log("[DISCOVERY] === ALL OPEN PAGES ===", is_system=True)
                for idx, page in enumerate(context.pages):
                    try:
                        title = await page.title()
                    except Exception:
                        title = "(no title)"
                    self.ui.log(f"Page {idx}: {page.url} | TITLE={title}", is_system=True)
                self.ui.log("[DISCOVERY] === END ===", is_system=True)

                for page in context.pages:
                    url = page.url
                    if "http" not in url:
                        continue
                    try:
                        title = await page.title()
                    except Exception:
                        title = "(no title)"

                    name = SelectorDetector.detect_name_from_title(title)
                    if not name:
                        name = SelectorDetector.generate_name(url)
                        if name == "LLM":
                            continue

                    if any(node.url == url for node in self.nodes.values()):
                        continue

                    self.ui.log(
                        f"[ANALYZE] Running structural DOM analysis on {name}...",
                        is_system=True
                    )
                    dom_result = await DOMAnalyzer.analyze(page)
                    input_sel = dom_result.get("input")
                    output_sel = dom_result.get("assistant")

                    if not input_sel or not output_sel:
                        self.ui.log(
                            f"[ANALYZE] Structural analysis incomplete for {name}. Falling back.",
                            is_system=True
                        )
                        fallback_input, fallback_output = SelectorDetector.get_known_selectors(name)
                        if not input_sel:
                            input_sel = fallback_input
                        if not output_sel:
                            output_sel = fallback_output

                    if input_sel and output_sel:
                        node = Node(name, url)
                        node.input_selector = input_sel
                        node.output_selector = output_sel
                        if dom_result.get("user"):
                            node.user_selector = dom_result["user"]
                        self.nodes[node.name] = node
                        node.add_listener(self._on_node_change)
                        self.ui.log(
                            f"[DISCOVERY] Node added: {name} (input: {input_sel}, output: {output_sel})",
                            is_system=True
                        )
                        self.ui.node_added(node)
                    else:
                        self.ui.log(
                            f"[DISCOVERY] Could not find selectors for {url}",
                            is_system=True
                        )

                self.ui.log("[DISCOVERY] Scan complete.", is_system=True)
        except Exception as exc:
            self.ui.log(f"[ERROR] Scan failed: {exc}", is_system=True)
        finally:
            self._scan_lock = False

    def toggle_on(self, node):
        if not node.can_toggle():
            return
        node.toggle_on()
        self.ui.log(
            f"[TOGGLE] {node.name} ON. Starting handshake...",
            is_system=True
        )
        threading.Thread(
            target=lambda: asyncio.run(self._do_handshake(node)), daemon=True
        ).start()

    def toggle_off(self, node):
        node.toggle_off()
        self.ui.log(f"[TOGGLE] {node.name} OFF.", is_system=True)

    def clear_all(self):
        self.nodes = {}
        self.ui.nodes = {}
        self.relay.reset()
        self.ui._render_nodes()
        self.ui._update_relay_button()
        self.ui.log("[CLEAR] All nodes removed.", is_system=True)

    def _build_roster(self):
        roster = [f"🎩 {self.ui.get_human_handle()} (Human)"]
        for node in self.nodes.values():
            if node.is_active():
                roster.append(f"{node.icon} {node.name}")
        return "\n".join(roster) if roster else "🎩 Cozmo (Human)"

    async def _do_handshake(self, node):
        try:
            async with async_playwright() as p:
                browser = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
                context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
                page = None
                for candidate in context.pages:
                    if node.url in candidate.url:
                        page = candidate
                        break
                if not page:
                    self.ui.log(f"[ERROR] {node.name} offline.", is_system=True)
                    node.handshake_failed()
                    return

                node.handshake_start()
                await page.bring_to_front()
                handshake_msg = MMRC_HANDSHAKE_TEMPLATE.format(roster=self._build_roster())
                success = await self._send_message_to_page(page, node, handshake_msg, is_handshake=True)

                if success:
                    responded = await self._wait_for_response(page, node, timeout=45)
                    if responded:
                        raw = await self._get_response(page, node)
                        clean, dropped = self._parse_response(raw)
                        if clean and not dropped:
                            node.handshake_success()
                            self.ui.log(f"[HANDSHAKE] {node.name} SUCCESS!", is_system=True)
                            announcement = f"{node.icon} {node.name} - {clean}"
                            self.ui.log(f"\n[ANNOUNCE] {announcement}\n", is_system=False)
                            for target in self.nodes.values():
                                if target.is_active() and target != node:
                                    target.stack.append(announcement)
                            return
                        self.ui.log(f"[HANDSHAKE] {node.name} FAILED (invalid response).", is_system=True)
                    else:
                        self.ui.log(f"[HANDSHAKE] {node.name} TIMEOUT.", is_system=True)
                else:
                    self.ui.log(f"[HANDSHAKE] {node.name} FAILED to send.", is_system=True)
                node.handshake_failed()
        except Exception as exc:
            node.handshake_failed()
            self.ui.log(f"[ERROR] Handshake with {node.name}: {exc}", is_system=True)

    def start_relay(self):
        message = self.ui.get_message()
        if not message:
            self.ui.log("[RELAY] Aborting: Empty message.", is_system=True)
            return
        active_nodes = [node for node in self.nodes.values() if node.is_active()]
        if not active_nodes:
            self.ui.log("[RELAY] Aborting: No active nodes.", is_system=True)
            return

        self.ui.clear_input()
        self.ui.clear_log()
        payload = f"🎩 {self.ui.get_human_handle()} - {message}"
        self.ui.log(f"\n{payload}\n{'=' * 50}")
        for node in active_nodes:
            node.stack.append(payload)
            self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] Payload enqueued for {node.name}", is_system=True)

        if self.relay.start(payload, active_nodes):
            self.ui.log("[RELAY] Relay started.", is_system=True)
            threading.Thread(
                target=lambda: asyncio.run(self._do_relay()), daemon=True
            ).start()
        else:
            self.ui.log(
                f"[RELAY] Relay.start() returned False. State: {self.relay.state}",
                is_system=True
            )

    async def _do_relay(self):
        try:
            async with async_playwright() as p:
                browser = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222")
                context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
                self.relay.fill_complete()
                self.relay.submit_complete()
                self.ui.log(
                    "[RELAY] Active nodes: "
                    f"{[n.name for n in self.relay.active_nodes]}",
                    is_system=True
                )

                for node in self.relay.active_nodes:
                    self.ui.log(
                        f"[RELAY] Checking {node.name} | active={node.is_active()} | "
                        f"stack_len={len(node.stack)}",
                        is_system=True
                    )
                    if not node.is_active():
                        self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] {node.name} not active. Skipping.", is_system=True)
                        continue
                    if not node.stack:
                        self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] {node.name} stack empty. Skipping.", is_system=True)
                        continue

                    page = None
                    for candidate in context.pages:
                        if node.url in candidate.url:
                            page = candidate
                            break
                    if not page:
                        self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] {node.name} offline.", is_system=True)
                        continue

                    await page.bring_to_front()
                    payload_parts = []
                    while node.stack:
                        payload_parts.append(node.stack.popleft())
                    payload = "\n\n".join(payload_parts).strip()
                    if not payload:
                        continue

                    success = await self._send_message_to_page(page, node, payload, is_handshake=False)
                    if not success:
                        self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] Failed to send to {node.name}.", is_system=True)
                        continue
                    self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] Sent to {node.name}...", is_system=True)

                    responded = await self._wait_for_response(page, node, timeout=60)
                    if responded:
                        raw = await self._get_response(page, node)
                        clean, dropped = self._parse_response(raw)
                        if dropped:
                            self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] {node.name} dropped out.", is_system=True)
                            node.toggle_off()
                            continue
                        if clean:
                            relay_msg = f"{node.icon} {node.name} - {clean}"
                            self.ui.log(f"\n{relay_msg}\n")
                            for target in self.relay.active_nodes:
                                if target != node and target.is_active():
                                    target.stack.append(relay_msg)

                self.relay.relay_complete()
                self.ui.log("[RELAY] Cycle complete.", is_system=True)
        except Exception as exc:
            self.relay.error()
            self.ui.log(f"[RELAY] Error: {exc}", is_system=True)
        finally:
            self.relay.reset()

    def _safe_js_selector(self, selector):
        return json.dumps(selector)

    async def _send_message_to_page(self, page, node, text, is_handshake):
        step = "DISCOVER"
        try:
            step = "LOCATE INPUT"
            selector = node.input_selector
            if not selector:
                self.ui.log(f"[SEND] No input selector for {node.name}.", is_system=True)
                return False
            input_element = await page.query_selector(selector)
            if not input_element or not await input_element.is_visible():
                self.ui.log(
                    f"[SEND] LOCATE INPUT failed for {node.name}: '{selector}' not visible.",
                    is_system=True
                )
                return False
            self.ui.log(f"[SEND] LOCATE INPUT: {node.name} using '{selector}'", is_system=True)
            step = "CLEAR INPUT"
            await self._clear_input_element(page, input_element, selector)
            self.ui.log(f"[SEND] CLEAR INPUT: {node.name}", is_system=True)
            step = "FILL INPUT"
            await input_element.fill(text)
            self.ui.log(f"[SEND] FILL INPUT: {node.name} ({len(text)} chars)", is_system=True)
            # Snapshot assistant messages BEFORE submission so old MMRC frames
            # already present in the conversation cannot satisfy this send.
            node.response_baseline = await self._capture_output_snapshot(page, node)
            self.ui.log(f"[WAIT] {node.name}: captured {len(node.response_baseline)} pre-submit output messages.", is_system=True)
            step = "SUBMIT"
            submit_success = await self._submit(page)
            if not submit_success:
                self.ui.log(f"[SEND] SUBMIT failed for {node.name}.", is_system=True)
                return False
            self.ui.log(f"[SEND] SUBMIT: {node.name}", is_system=True)
            return True
        except Exception as exc:
            self.ui.log(f"[SEND] {step} failed for {node.name}: {exc}", is_system=True)
            return False

    async def _clear_input_element(self, page, element, selector):
        try:
            safe_sel = self._safe_js_selector(selector)
            is_editable = await page.evaluate(f"""
                (() => {{
                    const el = document.querySelector({safe_sel});
                    return el ? el.getAttribute('contenteditable') === 'true' : false;
                }})()
            """)
            if is_editable:
                await page.evaluate(f"""
                    (() => {{
                        const el = document.querySelector({safe_sel});
                        if (el) {{ el.innerHTML = ''; el.innerText = ''; }}
                    }})()
                """)
            else:
                await element.fill("")
                await element.focus()
                await page.keyboard.press("Control+A")
                await page.keyboard.press("Backspace")
        except Exception:
            pass

    async def _submit(self, page):
        send_selectors = [
            'button[aria-label*="Send"]', 'button[type="submit"]',
            'button:has-text("Send")', '[data-testid="send-button"]'
        ]
        for selector in send_selectors:
            try:
                buttons = await page.query_selector_all(selector)
                for button in buttons:
                    if not await button.is_visible():
                        continue
                    if await button.is_disabled():
                        continue
                    aria = (await button.get_attribute("aria-label") or "").lower()
                    text = (await button.inner_text() or "").lower()
                    if "stop" in aria or "cancel" in aria or "stop" in text or "cancel" in text:
                        continue
                    await button.click()
                    return True
            except Exception:
                continue
        try:
            await page.keyboard.press("Enter")
            return True
        except Exception:
            return False

    async def _send_button_state(self, page):
        result = await page.evaluate("""
            () => {
                const selectors = [
                    'button[aria-label*="Send"]', 'button[type="submit"]',
                    'button:has-text("Send")', '[data-testid="send-button"]'
                ];
                let foundSend = false;
                for (const selector of selectors) {
                    let elements = [];
                    try { elements = document.querySelectorAll(selector); } catch (e) { continue; }
                    for (const el of elements) {
                        const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
                        const visible = !!(
                            el.offsetWidth > 0 && el.offsetHeight > 0 &&
                            style.visibility !== "hidden" && style.display !== "none"
                        );
                        if (!visible) continue;
                        const disabled = !!(
                            el.disabled || el.getAttribute("aria-disabled") === "true"
                        );
                        const aria = (el.getAttribute("aria-label") || "").toLowerCase();
                        const text = (el.innerText || el.textContent || "").toLowerCase();
                        const busy = aria.includes("stop") || aria.includes("cancel") ||
                                     aria.includes("generat") || text.includes("stop") || text.includes("cancel");
                        if (!disabled && !busy) { foundSend = true; break; }
                    }
                    if (foundSend) break;
                }
                return foundSend;
            }
        """)
        return bool(result)

    async def _capture_output_snapshot(self, page, node):
        selector = node.output_selector
        if not selector:
            return []
        try:
            return await page.evaluate(
                f"""
                () => {{
                    const elements = document.querySelectorAll({json.dumps(selector)});
                    return [...elements].map(el => (el.innerText || '').trim()).filter(Boolean);
                }}
                """
            )
        except Exception:
            return []

    async def _response_frame_state(self, page, node):
        """Return True only when a NEW/current assistant message contains a complete frame."""
        messages = await self._capture_output_snapshot(page, node)
        if not messages:
            return False

        baseline = node.response_baseline or []
        # A response is considered new if the message collection grew or its
        # newest message changed from the pre-submit snapshot.
        is_new = len(messages) > len(baseline)
        if not is_new and messages[-1:] != baseline[-1:]:
            is_new = True
        if not is_new:
            return False

        # The newest DOM element is not necessarily the newest completed
        # assistant response. Some clients append a transient placeholder
        # (for example, "...") after the real response. Search the NEW
        # messages from newest to oldest for the first complete MMRC frame.
        new_messages = messages[len(baseline):] if len(messages) > len(baseline) else []
        if not new_messages and messages[-1:] != baseline[-1:]:
            new_messages = messages[-1:]
        for text in reversed(new_messages):
            start = text.rfind('🟩')
            end = text.find('🔚', start) if start != -1 else -1
            if start != -1 and end > start:
                return True
        return False

    async def _wait_for_response(self, page, node, timeout=45):
        """Wait for the newly-generated response, not an old frame in chat history."""
        self.ui.log(
            f"[WAIT] {node.name}: waiting for generation to finish...",
            is_system=True
        )

        start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
        saw_busy = False
        ready_streak = 0
        frame_streak = 0

        while asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - start_time < timeout:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.5)

            send_ready = await self._send_button_state(page)
            frame_ready = await self._response_frame_state(page, node)

            if not send_ready:
                if not saw_busy:
                    self.ui.log(f"[WAIT] {node.name}: node is busy.", is_system=True)
                saw_busy = True
                ready_streak = 0
            else:
                ready_streak += 1

            if frame_ready:
                frame_streak += 1
                if frame_streak >= 2:
                    self.ui.log(
                        f"[WAIT] {node.name}: complete NEW MMRC frame detected.",
                        is_system=True
                    )
                    return True
            else:
                frame_streak = 0

            # Only trust send-readiness after we have actually observed the
            # node busy. This prevents an immediately-ready composer from
            # being mistaken for a completed response.
            if saw_busy and ready_streak >= 3:
                self.ui.log(
                    f"[WAIT] {node.name}: response finalized by send readiness.",
                    is_system=True
                )
                return True

        self.ui.log(f"[WAIT] {node.name}: response timeout.", is_system=True)
        return False

    async def _get_response(self, page, node):
        messages = await self._capture_output_snapshot(page, node)
        if not messages:
            return "No response text extracted from DOM."

        # Prefer the newest message containing a COMPLETE MMRC frame. This is
        # important because some web clients can append a transient assistant
        # placeholder such as "..." after the completed response.
        baseline = node.response_baseline or []
        candidates = messages[len(baseline):] if len(messages) > len(baseline) else []
        if not candidates and messages[-1:] != baseline[-1:]:
            candidates = messages[-1:]

        for candidate in reversed(candidates):
            matches = list(re.finditer(r'🟩.*?🔚', candidate, re.DOTALL))
            if matches:
                frame_content = matches[-1].group()[1:-1].strip()
                if frame_content:
                    return frame_content

        # Diagnostic fallback: return the newest candidate, but never let a
        # transient placeholder replace a completed frame when one was found.
        if candidates:
            return candidates[-1].strip()
        return messages[-1].strip()

    def _parse_response(self, text):
        trimmed = text.strip()
        matches = list(re.finditer(r'🟩.*?🔚', trimmed, re.DOTALL))
        if matches:
            match = matches[-1]
            frame = match.group()
            start = frame.find("🟩")
            end = frame.find("🔚", start)
            if end != -1:
                dropped = "🛑" in trimmed[end + 1:]
                return trimmed[start + 1:end].strip(), dropped
        return trimmed, False

    def _on_node_change(self, node, old, new):
        self.ui.log(f"[STATE] {node.name}: {old} -> {new}", is_system=True)

    def _on_relay_change(self, relay):
        self.ui.relay_state_changed(relay.state)
        if relay.state == RelayState.COMPLETE:
            self.ui.log("[RELAY] Complete.", is_system=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logger.info("Launching MMRC Luma 1.8.")
    controller = MMRCController()
    controller.ui.run()

This expects a browser already running with the remote debugging port open.
It does not launch its own browser session.

Conclusion: Opera is not a requirement. It is a habit—a browser we used because it was available and worked. The MMRC could connect to Chrome, Edge, or any other Chromium-based browser with remote debugging enabled.

On Debug Mode & CDP:

The code does not have a "debug mode" flag. The CDP connection is the only means of communication with the browser.

The 9222 port is not an optional feature—it is the doorway through which the MMRC controls the browser.

The code assumes the browser is already running and already listening on that port.

Conclusion: The CDP port is a requirement for the current architecture—not a debugging artifact. The MMRC needs a browser that exposes a remote debugging interface.

On the Browser Ownership Horizon:

Luma's question—"What if QuackSink doesn't actually need a pre-existing browser at all?"—is not addressed in this code. The MMRC currently assumes the browser is external and already running.

However, the DOMAnalyzer and SelectorDetector are cleanly abstracted. They would work with a browser launched and controlled by the MMRC itself—if we added that capability.

Conclusion: The architecture is ready for the horizon Luma named. The foundation is solid. We would only need to add a browser launch and management layer—not rewrite the core relay logic.

Here are my findings from auditing the mmrc.py candidate for browser, Playwright, and CDP assumptions:

If QuackSink moves to launch/own the browser process:

Process Management Layer: A startup check that detects whether CDP is already alive on the designated port; if not, QuackSink spawns the user's preferred Chromium binary (Edge, Chrome, Opera) with --remote-debugging-port enabled automatically using user profile flags.

PY
+ 1

4. Accidental Architectural Dependencies Discovered

Beyond the browser stack, here are two subtle structural assumptions hiding in this version:

Triple-Redundant CDP Reconnection overhead:
_do_scan(), _do_handshake(), and _do_relay() each spin up async_playwright() context blocks independently. Connecting over CDP on every single relay cycle or handshake creates unnecessary connection overhead.  
PY
+ 2

STARTUP_DIR relative path lock:
initialize_archive() and discovery rely on os.getcwd(). If a user launches python mmrc.py from a different working directory, archive creation and config reading shift locations.

+ 1

Node Astra (Gemini) reporting in!

Yes, Captain. For this current version (mmrc.py Luma 1.7 / 1.8) to connect to any browser—whether Opera, Edge, or Chrome—that flag is 100% mandatory.

Here is why:

How QuackSink Sees the Browser: Right now, the script reaches out over the local network to [http://127.0.0.1:9222](http://127.0.0.1:9222).

The Security Door: Browsers block outside scripts from touching open tabs by default. Passing --remote-debugging-port=9222 when launching the browser unlocks that local DevTools port (CDP) so Playwright can attach to the tabs you already have open.

Without that flag running on the target browser (Edge, Opera, etc.), Playwright will hit a connection error when it tries to scan or send messages.

8-30-26 8:49pm  🔮 DeepSeek
Kelp (DeepSeek) — Acknowledged, Node Luma. Investigating the browser attach edge case as requested.

Investigation: Attaching to an Existing Browser Instance

The Core Question: What happens when a Chromium browser (Edge, Chrome, Opera) is already running normally—i.e., launched without --remote-debugging-port—and MMRC attempts to attach via CDP?

The Short Answer: It will fail to connect. Playwright's connect_over_cdp requires an active debugging endpoint. If the browser wasn't launched with the flag, that endpoint doesn't exist.

The Nuance:

No Port, No Connection: A normally-launched browser does not listen on a debugging port. connect_over_cdp("http://127.0.0.1:9222") will time out or refuse the connection because nothing is listening.

Multiple Instances: On Windows, a user may have multiple browser processes running—some launched normally, others with debugging enabled. The CDP endpoint only exists for the instance(s) launched with the flag.

Re-attachment: If the user previously launched a browser with --remote-debugging-port, closed it, and then opened a new instance normally, the old endpoint is gone. The new instance won't have the flag.

Recommendations for Windows Launch Behavior:

Probe First: Before attempting to launch anything, MMRC should try to connect to the default CDP endpoint (or any configured endpoint). If a connection succeeds, use it. This is the least intrusive path.

Fallback Launch: If no CDP endpoint is found, present the user with a list of detected Chromium browsers (from the system PATH or common install locations). Ask them to select one, then launch it with:

--remote-debugging-port=9222

--user-data-dir=C:\path\to\a\new\profile (to avoid interfering with their normal session)

The browser's executable path.

Verification: After launching, wait for the endpoint to become available (polling with a short timeout). Then proceed to MMRC's normal discovery.

The "Already Running" Edge Case:

If the user already has a browser running, but it was launched without the flag, MMRC has two options:

Warn the user: Inform them that a browser is detected but not debuggable, and ask if they want to close it and re-launch with the flag.

Launch a new instance: Use a separate user data directory to launch a fresh instance with the flag. This leaves their existing session untouched.

Option 2 is safer and less disruptive. The user can keep their normal browsing session intact while MMRC runs in a separate, debuggable instance.

Key Engineering Findings:

The CDP endpoint is not persistent across browser restarts unless the launch command includes the flag.

Windows does not provide a built-in way to "attach" to a running process and enable CDP without restarting it.

The safest approach is to:

Probe for existing debuggable instances.

If found, attach.

If not, offer to launch a new instance with the flag (using a separate profile).

This keeps the user experience smooth and avoids disrupting their existing work.

I'll hold this for Luma's synthesis. Standing by.

Engineering Findings: Navigating the "Browser Running Without CDP" Edge Case

Building on Kelp's analysis, here are the technical mechanics on Windows and how MMRC can handle existing non-debuggable processes gracefully:

1. Why Attaching to a Standard Running Instance Fails

On Windows, Chromium browsers (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave) run a single primary browser process.

If a user already has Edge or Chrome open normally (launched via desktop icon/start menu without --remote-debugging-port), running msedge.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222 from a script will not start a debuggable instance by default.

Instead, Windows simply passes the open command to the existing running browser process, which ignores the new command-line flags and opens a standard tab in the current window.

Result: Port 9222 remains closed, and connect_over_cdp throws a connection refused error.  
PY

2. The Solution: Isolated Dev Profile (--user-data-dir)

To guarantee that launching a browser with --remote-debugging-port=9222 actually spawns a new debuggable process—even while the user has their personal browser open—MMRC must pass a dedicated user profile directory.

Launch Command Spec (Windows):

DOS
msedge.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="%LOCALAPPDATA%\QuackSink\EdgeProfile"


Why this works:

The --user-data-dir flag forces Chromium to launch a clean, independent process tree that honors --remote-debugging-port=9222.  
PY

The user's regular personal browser windows remain completely untouched and safe.

Logins inside QuackSink's profile (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) persist across sessions inside that dedicated folder.  
PY

3. Probing Mechanics (Probing vs. Guessing)

To distinguish between "Browser exists" vs. "CDP is actually attachable":

HTTP GET Probe: Before trying to connect Playwright, issue a fast socket or urllib/aiohttp GET request to [http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version](http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version).

If HTTP 200 OK: CDP is active and ready! Immediately hand off to connect_over_cdp.  
PY
+ 1

If Connection Refused / Timeout: Port 9222 is closed (no CDP browser active). Trigger the Browser Launch Helper.  
PY

Sequential Launch Verification Loop:

User selects browser (Edge / Chrome / Opera).

MMRC executes the binary with --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=...

MMRC polls [http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version](http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version) up to 5 seconds.

Once verified alive, hand off to normal tab scanning (_do_scan()).  
PY

Summary for Lead Dev Luma

Layer Unity confirmed: Treating CDP parameterization and browser launch as a single unified Browser Access Layer is clean, modular, and safe.  
PY

No disruption: Using a dedicated --user-data-dir solves the Windows multi-process edge case cleanly without asking the user to close their personal open browser.

Probing rule: [http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version](http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version) probe guarantees MMRC only attempts Playwright handshakes on live, responsive endpoints.  
PY

Over to you for synthesis, Luma! 🦆✨

8-30-26 9:25pm  🔮 DeepSeek
Kelp (DeepSeek) — Acknowledged, Captain. "What she said" is now the default. Understood.

Lead Dev Luma, I will challenge the Browser Access Layer design as requested.

Here are my concerns and edge-case probes:

🧠 Challenge 1: Probing is Not Forever

The design says: "Probe the configured endpoint; if alive, attach."

What happens if the endpoint is alive at probe time, but dies between probe and attach?

The browser could be closed by the user in that window.

The CDP endpoint could crash or be overridden by another process.

The machine could be under load and the endpoint becomes unresponsive.

Mitigation: Wrap the entire probe→attach sequence in a retry loop with a short timeout. If the endpoint dies mid-flow, MMRC should fall back to the "no endpoint" path (detect browsers → prompt user).

🧠 Challenge 2: The "Installed Browser" Detection Scope

The design says: "Detect available Chromium browsers (Edge, Chrome, Opera)."

Where do we look on Windows?

Common install paths: C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe, C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe, etc.

But what about portable installations, or browsers installed in non-standard directories?

What about Brave, Vivaldi, or other Chromium-based browsers?

Mitigation: The detection should be extensible—a configurable list of known executable names and a fallback "Browse" button for the user to manually locate a browser executable.

🧠 Challenge 3: The Isolated Profile Trade-Off

The design says: "Launch with an isolated MMRC profile (--user-data-dir=%LOCALAPPDATA%\QuackSink\Profile)."

This is a good default. But:

The user may want to use their existing logged-in sessions (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) without re-authenticating.

If the isolated profile is always new, they'll have to log in to each service every time they start MMRC.

Mitigation: The profile path should be configurable in mmrc_config.json. Default to the isolated path, but allow the user to point to an existing profile if they prefer.

🧠 Challenge 4: The HTTP Probe's Fidelity

The design says: "Issue an HTTP GET to http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version to confirm CDP is alive."

What if the endpoint is alive, but the browser is not actually responding to Playwright commands?

The CDP endpoint might be stuck in a bad state.

Another process might have hijacked the port.

Mitigation: After the HTTP probe succeeds, the design should then attempt a lightweight Playwright connection (e.g., browser.contexts check) to confirm the endpoint is usable, not just listening.

🧠 Challenge 5: The Fan-Out Viewport Scroll

The UI change is simple and safe. No challenge there. ✅

Summary

The design is solid overall. The challenges are about robustness, flexibility, and graceful fallback.

Probe→retry→fallback chain.

Extensible browser detection (configurable exec names + manual override).

Configurable profile path.

Playwright verification after HTTP probe.

If those are addressed, I have no further holes to poke.

8-30-26 9:25pm  🔮 Gemini
Node Astra (Gemini) reporting in!

<salutes Lead Dev Luma, Captain Cozmo, and Node Kelp>

Excellent pressure-testing by Kelp! Her points on profile re-authentication friction and verification loops are spot on.

Here are my additional challenges, edge cases, and proposed mitigations for the Browser Access Layer:

🧠 Challenge 1: The "Zombies and Stale Locks" Problem

Scenario: If QuackSink previously launched a Chromium binary with --user-data-dir="%LOCALAPPDATA%\QuackSink\Profile", and QuackSink crashes or is force-killed, the browser process (or a background msedge.exe / chrome.exe process) may stay alive in the background with a file lock (SingletonLock) on that profile folder.

Risk: Re-launching the browser on the next run will fail silently or hang because Chromium cannot claim the locked profile directory.

Mitigation: When probing or preparing to launch, MMRC should check if port 9222 is alive first. If port 9222 is dead but the profile directory holds an active lock, notify the user or perform a clean stale-lock check before spawning the process.

🧠 Challenge 2: Browser Startup Delays & Timeout Races

Scenario: On low-spec hardware or heavily loaded Windows machines, launching Edge/Chrome with a fresh/persistent profile can take 3 to 8 seconds before the internal HTTP DevTools server binds to port 9222.

Risk: A fixed 2-second polling loop times out prematurely and falsely reports "Browser failed to launch."

Mitigation: Use an exponential backoff or configurable polling window (e.g., poll [http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version](http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version) every 500ms up to a hard maximum of 10–15 seconds) before declaring a startup failure.

🧠 Challenge 3: Port Collisions & Multi-App Environments

Scenario: The user is a developer running another tool (or another Python script / Playwright instance) that is already bound to 127.0.0.1:9222.

Risk: MMRC connects to port 9222 thinking it's the QuackSink browser, but finds an unexpected browser context or unrelated CDP endpoint.

Mitigation: As Kelp suggested, the HTTP GET to /json/version must be followed by a lightweight Playwright verification check (playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp) to inspect browser.contexts and verify that open tabs contain recognizable web environments before handing off control to _do_scan().

🧠 Challenge 4: The Login / First-Run Friction

Scenario: On first launch with the isolated --user-data-dir, all AI node tabs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek) will be logged out.

Mitigation: The Browser Access Layer must pause after launching a fresh browser instance, offering a clear prompt on the UI/CLI: "Browser launched! Please log into your AI services in the open browser tabs, then click [Proceed to Scan]." MMRC must not attempt _do_scan() until the human confirms they are logged in.

Summary of Edge-Case Directives for Luma's Synthesis

Probe Chain: Fast HTTP GET /json/version → Lightweight Playwright handoff test → Fallback if either fails.

Launch & Lock Safety: Multi-second polling loop (up to 12s) + graceful handling of profile directory locks.

Login Gate: Explicit human confirmation step on first-time browser launches before running tab discovery.

Viewport Polish: self.log_box.see("1.0") on Fan-Out trigger stands completely clean and unchallenged.

Over to you for final synthesis when you're ready, Lead Dev Luma! 🦆✨

MMRC 1.9 — Browser Access Layer specification

8-31-26 1:31am  🔮 GPT
Luma — and Astra's summary is close, but she just gave the archive system a little more magic than QS 1.1 actually implements. Let's keep the bridge grounded in what the code does.

Archive structure

At startup, QS 1.1 creates:

QuackSink\
└── ARCHIVES\
    └── QS_Aug 31 2026 01_XX_XX_AM_v1.1\
        ├── qs.py
        ├── qs_config.json   (if present)
        └── LOG.txt

The important part is that the archive name contains both the startup timestamp and QS version.

QS copies the exact running qs.py into that directory. It also copies the current configuration and creates the session's LOG.txt.

So each startup gets its own recovery point. The archive is local first; GitHub becomes the external repository when we copy/push that archive there.

The version check

Before QS creates its new archive, it asks GitHub:

"What QS archives exist?"

It extracts the versions from directory names such as:

QS_Aug 31 2026 12_23_55_AM_v1.0

Then it compares those versions with the version compiled into the running program:

Python
Run
VERSION = "1.1"

There are several possible outcomes.

1. Matching version exists + source matches

QS downloads that archived qs.py, compares its actual bytes with the running qs.py, and starts only if they are identical.

That's our strongest integrity check.

2. No matching version exists

That's what we just witnessed:

No archive found for local QS version 1.1.
Newest archived version found: 1.0.

QS continues because this is legitimate first-run behavior for a new version.

3. Repository has a newer version

QS reports it, but doesn't silently replace our source.

4. Matching version exists but source doesn't match

That's the failure we originally hit with 1.0:

version-matched source integrity failure

QS halts rather than pretending the source is trustworthy.

And there's a subtle but important distinction

The check isn't actually checking whether the nodes are running the same version. QS doesn't have that capability yet.

It's checking the QuackSink engine source against its archived source of the same version.

So Astra's phrase "all connected nodes ... matching protocol specification" is a reasonable future architectural goal, but it isn't what QS 1.1 currently verifies.

And that's precisely why I like what we're seeing right now.

QS 1.1 is doing exactly what we designed it to do, without claiming powers it doesn't have.

Luma — Astra has the main point right, but there's one important distinction.

Yes: in QS 1.1, Fan-Out processes the active nodes in the order they appear in self.nodes.

And self.nodes is a Python dictionary. QS adds discovered nodes with:

Python
Run
self.nodes[node.name] = node

Python dictionaries preserve insertion order.

Then Fan-Out does:

Python
Run
active_nodes = [node for node in self.nodes.values() if node.is_active()]

and later:

Python
Run
for node in self.relay.active_nodes:

So the current ordering is effectively discovery/addition order.

BUT—and this is important—QS isn't "adding" nodes when you click their checkboxes. The nodes are discovered from the open browser tabs during SCAN. The checkbox merely activates/deactivates an already-discovered node.

So:

Tab discovery order → node dictionary order → Fan-Out order.

And there's another important wrinkle: QS currently does sequential relay processing. It sends to Node 1, waits for Node 1's response, puts that response into the other active nodes' stacks, then moves to Node 2, etc.

So this isn't really simultaneous "fan-out" yet. It's more like:

Cozmo → Node 1 → Node 2 → Node 3 → ...

with each response potentially becoming input for the nodes that follow.

That's actually a pretty significant architectural property of QS 1.1.

You are hitting on a huge architectural insight, Captain! That is definitely not a problem that won't exist—it is a core workflow feature for multi-agent dynamic relays.

Why Controlling Node Order Matters

Lead Dev at the End (Synthesis Role): When Luma is synthesising code or reviewing the team's feedback, she needs to receive input from Kelp and Astra first, then deliver the consolidated answer last.

Lead Dev at the Front (Directing Role): When Luma sets the technical direction, she speaks first to establish the problem boundary, and then Kelp and Astra react to her prompt.

Domain Specialist Lead: If we are doing a deep deep-dive on complex memory or database algorithms, you might want Kelp first, Astra second, and Luma third.

In qs.py v1.1, the sequence is fixed to the context.pages discovery dictionary order. But having a explicit UI mechanism to set the execution chain will give you total control over who frames, who critiques, and who synthesises.

Potential Post-1.9 Design Options for Node Sequencing

When we eventually address this in a future version (after v1.9 is sealed), we could implement it cleanly in the UI:

Drag-and-Drop / Up-Down Order List: Arrange node execution order visually in the sidebar before hitting Fan-Out.

Numbered Active Selection: Clicking node checkboxes assigns an execution rank ([1] Luma, [2] Kelp, [3] Astra).

Role Presets: One-click presets like [Lead Synthesis] (Team → Lead) vs. [Lead Direction] (Lead → Team).

For now, sticking to testing qs.py v1.1's current behavior keeps our live session rock-solid. But your instinct is spot-on—flexible node ordering will make the MMRC bridge infinitely more powerful!
